name: Can you add an ADU to a custom floor plan in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Can a custom floor plan be developed to include an ADU, guest house, or duplex-style arrangement on the same property?
mainEntity.text: Can a custom floor plan be developed to include an ADU, guest house, or duplex-style arrangement on the same property?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, an ADU or guest house can be integrated into a custom floor-plan strategy, but the site must be designed as a whole. The main house, secondary unit, parking, entry paths, utility routing, and privacy buffers all affect the layout. On many Los Angeles properties, the best solution is to design the primary residence and ADU together so they share a coherent site plan and do not create conflicts later. This is especially important when the lot is small, narrow, or already constrained by existing structures. A good custom plan will consider how residents enter both units, where windows are placed for privacy, and whether the ADU should be attached, detached, or above garage level. It should also be evaluated against local zoning, setbacks, and fire/access requirements before details are finalized. If the ADU is added too late in the process, the main home may need to be redesigned to preserve usable outdoor space and compliance.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. A custom floor plan can be developed to integrate an ADU, guest suite, or secondary unit, but the layout must account for setbacks, access, privacy, parking, and separate circulation. The design should be planned as one site strategy, not as two disconnected buildings.
